verdict.rationale: Grok Build is itself a coding agent, so it plays the MCP client role, and serving tools to other agents through an official MCP server is a different product role. The evidence shows only client-side MCP support (`grok mcp add`, loading `.mcp.json` and other MCP configs), which belongs to the separate MCP-client story and is not credited here. Its ACP JSON-RPC mode is a different protocol, not an MCP server mode, so nothing shows the agent runs as an MCP server.
